newsitem.title: UK: Camelot suffers loss to bookies in UK lottery row.
newsitem.headline: Camelot suffers loss to bookies in UK lottery row.

text.p: A UK High Court judge on Tuesday denied lottery operator Camelot the right to challenge the legality of a fixed odds numbers game run by bookmakers.
Camelot argued that the 49's game constituted an illegal lottery and was seeking a judicial review of the Department of Public Prosecutions' decision to take no action against it.
However, Mr Justice Ognall refused the application in the High Court. Camelot can now either appeal against the High Court decision or seek a private prosecution.
The 49's game was was set up by bookmakers Coral, Ladbroke and William Hill in December.

It has been introduced to counter the effects on bookmakers of the National Lottery. The bookmakers have been lobbying for the right to take side bets on the Lottery but the government has so far resisted their calls.
They face intensified competition from the Lottery after last week's introduction of a midweek draw.
In the 49's game, customers can bet on between one and five numbers in a daily draw, odds ranging from 11/2 on picking one number to 99,999/1 for all five.

Bookmakers note that the independent Henley Centre has forecast the midweek draw will further depress their turnover by an annualised 3.2 percent. The betting industry estimates that 49's will generate some three percent of betting turnover.
Bookmakers argue that 49s is helping the betting industry to retain customers, keep marginal shops open and save jobs.
